guards.title: Escape inside the open access menu closes only the menu
guards.goal: The first Escape closes the menu and keeps the dialog open

plan.root_cause: The dropdown's Escape key handler unconditionally preventsDefault and stopsPropagation, swallowing the Escape event even when the dropdown menu is closed. This prevents the modal's Escape listener from receiving the event to close the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler to only preventDefault/stopPropagation and clear menus when Escape is pressed and the dropdown menu is shown. When the menu is not shown, allow the Escape event to propagate so the modal can handle it.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will now close the share modal when focus is on the access toggle button, enabling keyboard users to dismiss the dialog as expected.
functional_risks: Escape may no longer clear dropdown menus when the menu is closed (but this is acceptable as the menu is already closed).
Potential side effects if other components rely on the dropdown consuming Escape events universally; however, the change only affects Escape when the menu is not shown.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape with focus on the access toggle button closes the share modal.
Verify that pressing Escape with the dropdown menu open closes only the menu (does not close the modal).
Verify that ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter interactions with the dropdown remain functional.
Verify that Escape still closes the modal when focus is elsewhere in the modal (e.g., on the Cancel or Save buttons).

plan.root_cause: The dropdown's Escape key handler unconditionally calls preventDefault() and stopPropagation() before checking if the menu is actually open. This swallows the Escape event even when the dropdown menu is closed, preventing the modal's Escape listener from receiving the event to close the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Restructure the dataApiKeydownHandler to check if the dropdown menu is active (isActive) before handling Escape. Only call preventDefault/stopPropagation and clearMenus when Escape is pressed AND the menu is shown. When the menu is not shown, return early without preventing default, allowing the event to propagate to the modal.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will now close the share modal when focus is on the access toggle button and the dropdown menu is closed. When the dropdown menu is open, Escape will close only the menu (not the modal), preserving expected dropdown behavior.
functional_risks: Escape key behavior changes only when dropdown menu is closed; menu-open behavior unchanged.
Other components relying on dropdown consuming Escape events universally may be affected, but this aligns with APG pattern where Escape closes the current component only.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape with focus on the access toggle button (menu closed) closes the share modal.
Verify that pressing Escape with the dropdown menu open closes only the menu (does not close the modal).
Verify that ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter interactions with the dropdown remain functional.
Verify that Escape still closes the modal when focus is elsewhere in the modal (e.g., on the Cancel or Save buttons).
